title: Daylight Saving Checker: Is DST in Effect?
description: Check whether daylight saving applies at a place with the Daylight Saving Checker — standard and daylight offsets from timezone rules. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, in 2026 US daylight saving runs from March 8 to November 1, while most of Europe runs March 29 to October 25 — three weeks of the year when the usual offset between them is wrong.
quick_answer: The Daylight Saving Checker compares a location's standard and daylight-saving offsets using the timezone rules for that place. Pick a place and a time context and read whether DST applies there and when it starts and ends — 'spring forward' is a local law, not a world event.
steps_intro: DST is a rule with a geography. Check the place, not the rumour:

body.t: Calls land wrong in the changeover weeks. Check both ends before fixing a recurring time — the
builds the overlap from the same rules.
A flight itinerary printed in local times hides the night the clocks move. Know your destination's dates before you set the alarm.
Systems that assume fixed offsets break twice a year. The checker's rules are the same tz-database rules your servers should be using.
Some places simply do not observe DST — most of Arizona (the Navajo Nation excepted) and Hawaii among them. The checker answers per place, which is the only honest way.

In 2026 the US starts DST on March 8 and Europe on March 29. For those three weeks New York is 5 hours behind London instead of the usual 6 — the fortnight in which a thousand standing calls quietly shift.

Australia's daylight saving runs through the northern winter (roughly October to April). Sydney's offset difference with London swings by two hours across the year, in the opposite direction to the US swing.

faq: It follows the timezone database's rules, which cover the world's zones including their historical quirks. Exclaves and oddities are the database's daily bread.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — pick any place on earth. Your location is only used if you ask another tool for it.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Timezone boundaries are political and revise occasionally; the tz database tracks them, and other sources may lag a change.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
United States: March 8. Europe: March 29. The table on this page holds the main regions' 2026 dates under current rules.
Why do the US and Europe change on different dates?
Separate laws, separate Sundays. The gap weeks are when transatlantic offsets are an hour off their usual values.
Debated in the US and EU for years; as of the current rules, it continues. The checker applies the rules in force, not the debate.
